answer: The trellis multiplier is published, charged in copper, and garden lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3874 identities would post 695 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
